rows.jp: 夜が暑苦しくないのが、田舎のいいとこだ。
rows.en: One good thing about the country was that the nights weren’t stifling.

rows.jp: 窓から滑り込む風はほどよく冷たく、肌に優しい。
rows.en: The breeze slipping through the window was pleasantly cool and gentle on my skin.

rows.jp: 今日は書き物がいっぱいだ。
rows.en: I had a lot of writing to do tonight.

ghs.en: There's lots to write today.

rows.jp: 日記はもちろん、原稿も書かないと。
rows.en: Not just my diary. I had the script too.

ghs.en: The diary, of course, but I also got to do the script.
ghs.assessment: The source says he also has to write the broadcast script. 'Do the script' is an imprecise collocation that omits the named act of writing.
ghs.remedy: Say that he has to write the script.

rows.jp: 原稿から片づけるか。
rows.en: I’d get the script out of the way first.

ghs.en: I think I'll get things done starting from the script.

rows.jp: 「……ふーむ」

ghs.en: Taichi: "...uh huh."
ghs.assessment: The source is a thoughtful 'Hmm' while he considers what to write. 'Uh huh' conventionally signals agreement or acknowledgment and changes the speech function.
ghs.remedy: Use a pondering interjection such as 'Hmm.'

rows.jp: 初回放送にふさわしい文面、か。
rows.en: Wording fit for an inaugural broadcast.

ghs.en: Suitable content for the pilot broadcast, then.
Taichi: "......"

rows.jp: 難。
rows.en: Difficult.

ghs.en: {}DIFFICULT.
ghs.assessment: The source is a terse declaration that the task is difficult. The English preserves the word but leaks empty control or formatting braces into visible text.

rows.jp: 書いては消し、書いては消し。
rows.en: Write, erase. Write, erase.

ghs.en: Write then erase then write then erase.

rows.jp: 一進一退の攻防。
rows.en: A battle that advanced and retreated by turns.

ghs.en: Offense and defense in an advance and retreat.
ghs.assessment: The source figuratively describes a back-and-forth struggle that makes no progress. The word-for-word military nouns do not form that idiom in English.
ghs.remedy: Use a natural image of a back-and-forth struggle.

highlights.text: Offense and defense in an advance and retreat

rows.jp: 一時間後、机に突っ伏す。
rows.en: An hour later, I collapsed across the desk.

ghs.en: One hour later, I fall prostate on the desk.
ghs.assessment: The source says he slumps face down onto the desk. 'Prostate' names a gland; the intended posture word is 'prostrate,' and even that needs the desk relation stated clearly.
ghs.remedy: Say that he slumps face down over the desk.

rows.jp: おいおい、進んだの二行だけだよ。
rows.en: Come on. I’d only managed two lines.

ghs.en: Come on, come ooon, I only gained two lines!

rows.jp: 『我々は、群青学院放送部である。この放送域はただいま我らによって占拠された。全員すみやかに武装を放棄し―――』
rows.en: “We are the Gunjo Academy Broadcasting Club. This broadcast zone is now under our occupation. All personnel will immediately lay down their arms and—”

ghs.en:
『We are known as the Gunjou Institute Broadcast
Club. The area within the range of this broadcast
has presently become our exclusive possession.
All present must speedily discard their armaments
and---』

rows.jp: 「ダメだダメだ！」
rows.en: “No, no!”

ghs.en: Taichi: "No, no and no!"

rows.jp: 原稿用紙を破り捨てる。
rows.en: I tore up the page.

ghs.en: I tear up the Japanese writing paper with its neat squares, and toss it.

rows.jp: 受けを狙いすぎて、全然趣旨から外れてしまっているっっっ！
rows.en: I’d chased the laugh so hard that I had missed the point entirely!!!

ghs.en: I aimed too far towards playing to the crowd and trying to get laughs, and totally got off the poooint!

rows.jp: 真面目でいいんだ。
rows.en: Serious would be fine.

ghs.en: Better do this seriously.

rows.jp: ちょっと微妙なおもしろみを加えようとして、おかしくなった。
rows.en: I’d tried to add a subtle touch of humor, and the whole thing had come out weird.

ghs.en: I went to add too much subtle funny on it, and it just got weird.
ghs.assessment: The source says a slight attempt to add an uncertain bit of humor made the draft strange. The English treats 'funny' as a mass noun and uses the wrong preposition.
ghs.remedy: Say that trying to add a subtle bit of humor made it strange.

highlights.text: too much subtle funny on it

rows.jp: 「やめだ」
rows.en: “Forget it.”

ghs.en: Taichi: "I quit."

rows.jp: 今夜は気分が乗らない。
rows.en: I wasn’t feeling it tonight.

ghs.en: This evening I just can't get into the mood.

rows.jp: 日記を書こう。
rows.en: I’d write my diary.

ghs.en: Let's write the diary.

rows.jp: 感情を対象化せよ！
rows.en: Objectify emotion!

ghs.en: Make those emotions objective!

rows.jp: カレーパンのカレーをごはんにかけて食べだしたのは誰なんだろう？
rows.en: Who first decided to scoop the curry out of a curry bun and eat it over rice?

ghs.en:
Who was it that first took the curry out of
the curry bread and ate that with rice?

rows.jp: そんな疑問が、いつも僕を差違なむ。%N※差違なむ＝太一の誤字。苛むという意味を、差違による違和感と結びつけた論理的な間違い。
rows.en: Questions like this always discrepain me.%N*“Discrepain” is Taichi’s error: he mistakenly combines the pain of being tormented with the discomfort of a discrepancy.

rows.jp: 太一は同様にタートルネックをトータルネックと間違えて認識しており、首をトータルに包むからトータルネックなのだと今なおかたく信じている。
rows.en: Likewise, Taichi believes “turtleneck” is “total-neck,” because it totally covers the neck, and remains firmly convinced of this even now.

ghs.en:
Similarly, due to having mistaken 'turtleneck'
for 'totalneck', to this day Taichi firmly
believes the name 'totalneck' must come
from how the sweater totally encloses
the neck.

rows.jp: わかたれることのない路を、幾度となく繰り返し往腹してきた、日々の終わりにわずかなりともむなしさを感じてならない。%N※往腹＝太一の誤字
rows.en: At the end of days spent making the same indivisible journey back and stomach again and again, I cannot help but feel at least a little empty.%N*“Back and stomach” is Taichi’s error for “back and forth.”

rows.jp: ボードレールは言った。
rows.en: Baudelaire said,

ghs.en: Baudelaire said this:

rows.jp: 『神は死んだ』と。
rows.en: “God is dead.”

ghs.en: 『God is dead.』

rows.jp: 神の存在を疑うことはたやすいが、神の悪戯というものは存在し否応もなく人生に降り注ぎ毎日通う路にも似て直線的であると信じていた人生に、突如として分岐点を儲けようとするのだ。%N※儲けよう＝太一の誤字
rows.en: It is easy to doubt God’s existence, but divine mischief does exist, raining irresistibly down upon our lives and suddenly trying to profit a fork in a life we had believed to be as straight as the road we walk each day.%N*“Profit a fork” is Taichi’s error for “provide a fork.”

ghs.en:
But to doubt the existence of God is to take
things simply, for in a life believed to be as
linear as the straightest of roads, where the
days are lived giving no assent and denial
neither to this existence, what is known as a
Prank of God will yet with a sudden profit
carrefours.
* Profit[sic] = prepare

rows.jp: たとゑば教室で、意固地な女性と無毛な会話を繰り広げた時。%N※無毛＝不毛の間違い
rows.en: For ensample, when I engaged a stubborn woman in a hairless conversation in the classroom.%N*“Hairless” is Taichi’s error for “fruitless.”

rows.jp: たとゑば廓下で、仲の良い友人と疎遠な友人のふたりに同時に会った時。
rows.en: For ensample, when I met a close friend and an estranged friend at the same time in the hallway.

rows.jp: そしてまたその二人同士が友好的な関係を築いていたとき。
rows.en: And when those two friends had themselves established a friendly relationship.

rows.jp: 私はそのどちらに対しても、×××（塗りつぶされている）の屹立する意志を感じずにはいられずまた彼女たちが等しく有する神秘の××××で×××に鼻寄せ口つけて××××の際には惜しみない愛とともにあるのであり――
rows.en: Toward each of them, I cannot help but feel the towering will of ××× (blacked out); moreover, with the mysterious ×××× they equally possess, I draw my nose near ×××, press my lips to it, and in the hour of ×××× am accompanied by unstinting love――

rows.jp: 『語りえないことについては、沈黙しなければならない』%Nこれはキルケゴールの有名な言葉だ。
rows.en: “Whereof one cannot speak, thereof one must be silent.”%NThis is a famous saying by Kierkegaard.

rows.jp: 霧嬢の奥ゆかしい中性美と、それに対する私の正当なる熱情についての言及は、ここまでにしておこう。
rows.en: Let this suffice for discussion of Kiri’s demure androgynous beauty and my entirely proper passion for it.

ghs.en:
Allusions to Kiri-jou's modest androgyny,
and the just ardor this one has with regards
to the said, shall be left with this.

rows.jp: 人生の喜びはこれだけではないのだから。
rows.en: For this is not the only joy in life.

ghs.en:
Allusions to Kiri-jou's modest androgyny,
and the just ardor this one has with regards
to the said, shall be left with this.

rows.jp: そう。
rows.en: Indeed.

ghs.en: Hence.
ghs.assessment: The source is an affirming transition equivalent to 'Yes' or 'That's right.' 'Hence' asserts a logical consequence that the one-word source does not encode.

rows.jp: 屋上で出会った我が人生の先達であり、母なる包容力をもってして接し慈しんでくれる見里嬢については、いくら書いたとしても私腹は尽きない。%N※私腹＝太一の誤字
rows.en: As for Misato, the guide of my life whom I met on the roof, who enfolds and cherishes me with a mother’s boundless compassion, no amount of writing could exhaust my paper profits.%N*“Paper profits” is Taichi’s error for “space on the page.”

rows.jp: まず何と言っても太も（以下、検閲）
rows.en: First and foremost, her thi—(remainder censored)

ghs.en:
First, whatever I may say, her so plump
thigh(remainder under censorship review)

rows.jp: そして私の手には、彼女の身につけていた胸布が残された。
rows.en: And in my hand remained the breast-cloth she had worn.

rows.jp: すでに体温の失われたそれを介して呼吸をする時、仄かな少女の%Nスメルは私をまたたくまに幻想的な幻想へと連れ去るのであっ%Nた。
rows.en: When I breathed through it after its warmth had faded, the faint maiden’s%Nscent swept me away in an instant to a fantastical fantasy, and so it%Nwas.

ghs.en:
On the moment of a respiratory act through the
item already parting with that warmth by body
induced, the faint subodorare of young woman in
an instant whisks me into a delusional world of
delusional delusion.
~FIN~

rows.jp: ～ＦＩＮ～
rows.en: ~FIN~

rows.jp: 決まった。
rows.en: Nailed it.

ghs.en: It is accomplished.

rows.jp: 詩情に溢れかつ哲学的。
rows.en: Brimming with poetry and philosophy.

ghs.en: It is overflowing with poetry and furthermore philosophical,

rows.jp: 芸術の都ロンドンに生まれていればスターダム確実の文才がほとばしった。
rows.en: Had I been born in London, city of art, this torrent of literary talent would have guaranteed me stardom.

ghs.en: a surge of authentic literary talent that if I had been born in that capital of the fine arts London, stardoming would've been the foregone.
ghs.assessment: The source boasts that stardom would have been assured had he been born in London. The English invents the verb 'stardoming' and leaves 'foregone' without the noun needed for the idiom.
ghs.remedy: Say that stardom would have been a foregone conclusion.

rows.jp: いやあ、ただ小難しい言葉を使うだけで、気取れるものだなあ。
rows.en: Amazing how simply using difficult words could make a man sound sophisticated.

ghs.en: Naaah, 'tis just a put on airs mine, I'm just using tortuous verbiage here!
ghs.assessment: The source admits that merely using difficult words makes it easy to sound pretentious. The English phrase has no grammatical subject-predicate structure and mangles the idiom 'put on airs.'
ghs.remedy: Use a grammatical admission that difficult words alone let him sound pretentious.

highlights.text: 'tis just a put on airs mine

rows.jp: タームとかトートロジーとかアイロニーとか、そういう専門用語も決して平易な日本語に訳すことなくバンバン使っていかないとな。
rows.en: Words like term, tautology, and irony—I had to fling technical jargon around without ever translating it into plain Japanese.

ghs.en: Weltanschaaung, countenancing, intratextuality: those are the kind of technical terms that I got to use like bullets in a machine gun without translation into plain language.
ghs.assessment: The source specifically lists 'term,' 'tautology,' and 'irony' as jargon he should deploy untranslated. The English replaces all three examples, misspells one substitute, and includes a nontechnical ordinary word.
ghs.remedy: Preserve the source's three example terms.

rows.jp: 「んっ」
rows.en: “Ngh.”

ghs.en: Taichi: "Nnnh..."

rows.jp: 伸びをしてリラックスする。
rows.en: I stretched and relaxed.

ghs.en: I have a stretch and relax.

rows.jp: 作家というのも悪くない。
rows.en: Being a writer wasn’t half bad.

ghs.en: Being a writer's not bad.

rows.jp: ちょっと現代日本では過激すぎて検閲した部分もあるが。
rows.en: Some of it had been a little too radical for modern Japan, so I had censored those parts.

ghs.en: It's unfortunate that there are parts too extreme for modern day Japan which needed to be censored.

rows.jp: そうだ、原稿もこのノリで行こう。
rows.en: That was it. I’d write the script in this same spirit.

ghs.en: Right, let's go with the same feeling for the script.

rows.jp: ペダントリーの装飾をもって絢爛たる放送絵巻を綴りだし、知識階級の聞き物たる高尚かつ繊細な原稿にしてみせる。
rows.en: I would ornament it with pedantry, unspooling a sumptuous panorama of broadcasting into a lofty and delicate script fit for the listening pleasure of the intellectual class.

ghs.en: I shall embroider a dazzlingly flowery Broadcast Picture Scroll with pedantry as its ornament, and output an advanced and furthermore subtle script worthy of being heard by the intelligentsia.

rows.jp: 俄然やる気になって、再びペンを取った。
rows.en: Suddenly inspired, I picked up my pen again.

ghs.en: Inspiration struck in a sudden, and once again I took to the pen.
ghs.assessment: The source says he suddenly becomes motivated and takes up his pen again. English requires 'all of a sudden' or a direct adverb, and 'inspiration struck' shifts motivation toward receiving an idea.
ghs.remedy: Say that he suddenly felt motivated and picked up the pen again.
